rv.q: Emma Rice’s version of the ancient Cornish myth is a real heartbreaker, and there can be no better place to enjoy it than at the Minack.
A beautiful balance of love and hate, Killology is both disturbing and life-affirming.

While Killology can be far from comfortable viewing, it features good performances, particularly from Richard Mylan, and has the ability to make viewers think deeply about some important issues facing us all today.
A slippery drama with a strong moral core, it pits long-term care against short-term capitalism and, ultimately, ends up stating the obvious.
Oscillations of violence and begotten tenderness vibrate into a terrible empathy for both.

cn.t: Owen's dark, disturbing drama earns praise for its strong moral examination of violence and gaming culture, with critics highlighting the powerful playwright-director partnership and raw, compelling storytelling.
